turns.text: Hey Lloyd, did that package with the thermal paste arrive?
I don't see a tracking update for a thermal paste order in your recent emails. Did you check the spam folder?
No, just checking. Anyway, I've been diving into pathfinding algorithms for my game prototype.
That sounds interesting. Are you using A* or something more dynamic?
I'm looking at collision avoidance. Specifically, I found that Optimal Reciprocal Collision Avoidance (ORCA) is a canonical method for velocity-space conflict resolution.
That is a well-known approach for multi-agent navigation. It usually handles local avoidance very well.
Yeah, it seems robust. I might implement a basic version of it this weekend.
Good luck! Let me know if you need help with the math.
Lloyd, what's the weather like for Saturday?
It's looking partly cloudy with a high of 75°F. Good for hiking.
Nice. I might cancel the hike and stay in to code. I'm still tweaking my agent movement logic.
Sticking with the collision avoidance work?
Yes. I realized ORCA linearizes RVO constraints and operates in O(n) per agent via 2D linear programs.
That efficiency is definitely a key selling point for real-time applications.
Exactly. The computational cost is manageable compared to other global planners.
Makes sense. Let me know if you hit any performance bottlenecks.
